De Anglia invadenda quod objicitur: Æternum
Deum, cui cordium nostrorum intimi recessus ex-
plorati sunt, testamur, nunquam nobis in mentem
yenisse, ullam gentem damno quolibet afficere,
multo minus vicinam Angliam, cum qua in eadem
insula, sub eodem rege, remotis omnibus contro-
versiis, & exhibitis tot sinceri amoris indiciis hacte-
nus degimus, ut sperari vix posset, illud unquam
eventurum inter gentes sibi invicem olim tam ad-
versas, nunc vero feliciter reconciliatas, ac arctissi-
mis vinculis conjunctas, quibus potius arctius con-
stringendis, quam iniqua hostilitate dissecandis stu-
debimus. Atque licet confidamus, ipsa hujus con-
tra nos calumniæ improbabilitate, apud bonos fi-
dem omnem obstructum iri; ut tamen improbis
hisce calumniatoribus os obstruatur, ac pudore, si
quis illis reliquus sit, suffundantur, gravamina &
metus, conatus & proposita nostra ea libertate &
sinceritate breviter delineabimus, qua demonstrari
possit quam amice in fratres Anglos feramur, ac va-
nitas & falsitas calumniæ hujus omnium oculis obji-
ciantur.

page.notes: Page is a single running text column; no marginal notes printed in the text block. Left-edge marks and show-through from the reverse side are not transcribed. "narum" at the line start is a fragment (earum), kept as printed. "yenisse" is printed with y (venisse) and is kept as printed. The word "proposita" in the text contains a Cyrillic-looking letter in the transcription; the printed word is "proposita" and should be read with Latin letters only.
